title: Outside contribution: review and squash-merge the stacked natural-sort PRs #604 -> #605 -> #606 (DEC-181; issue #603)
description: DEC-181 (quest-cli, first case). Three open PRs from the fork Aztec03hub (Phil LaFayette), all base dev, all fixing the same id-ordering defect, stacked and overlapping on src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts and test/task-id-natural-sort.test.ts: #604 https://github.com/opum-ai/quest-cli/pull/604 closes issue #603 https://github.com/opum-ai/quest-cli/issues/603 (order task ids by number; +146/-21, 7 files); #605 https://github.com/opum-ai/quest-cli/pull/605 (draft and cleanup ids by number; +229/-25, 8 files); #606 https://github.com/opum-ai/quest-cli/pull/606 (a milestone task ids in numeric order; +213/-23, 9 files). Measured 2026-10-13: all three are MERGEABLE and BLOCKED only by held workflow runs -- GitHub holds the workflow runs of a first-time contributor, so no check has reported. maintainerCanModify is true on all three. Ruled by opum-doc DEC-181: (2) read the WHOLE diff and confirm it touches no .github/, package.json scripts or dependencies, lockfile, build or test-runner config, or install hooks before approving any run; (4) squash-merge with credit, never re-implement and close; (5) technical-only comments with a fixed disclosure line; (7) handle #604 first, then #605 and #606 in stack order. A separate sonnet reviewer runs the whole-diff check by ref; this session never checks out or runs fork code locally. The contributor never needs to touch .quest.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The three PRs are handled in stack order #604 then #605 then #606, and each is acknowledged on the PR within one working day.

Before any held workflow run is approved for a PR, the whole diff of that PR is confirmed to touch no .github/, no package.json scripts or dependencies, no lockfile, no build or test-runner configuration, and no install hooks; a PR touching any of those goes to opum-doc without approving runs.
Each PR is squash-merged, preserving the contributor authorship on the commit, only once its required check set is green on that exact head SHA and the reviewer has approved that same head SHA.
No fork code is checked out or run on a fleet machine outside CI.
Every comment posted on a PR is technical only and ends with the line: Reviewed by an AI agent working for the Opum maintainers.
Each PR outcome (merged, or changes requested) is reported to opum-agent, and the contributor is never asked to edit .quest.

(2) and (3) filed as QCLI-498 for the maintainers.

Progress, 2026-10-13, opus session (claude-opus-5-5, model verified by team-lead from transcript). HELD on the contributor's rebase of #605 and #606.

VERDICTS (accepted by team-lead): #605 APPROVE on merit at head 9684e294d82a9859a664f828bae19d31d81061b7; #606 APPROVE on merit at head 867d88e16260b21daf42036b34a28d84af818722. Required set (source-gates, Tracker integrity, lore check) all success on both heads. Both are CONFLICTING with dev since #604 squashed as a28c8182 (taskIdSortKey docblock, CHANGELOG insertion point); update-branch cannot resolve an add/add conflict, so a rebase was requested:
- #605: https://github.com/opum-ai/quest-cli/pull/605#issuecomment-6144556262 (rebase onto dev keeping only 9684e29)
- #606: https://github.com/opum-ai/quest-cli/pull/606#issuecomment-6144557404 (rebase after #605 lands keeping 0d3ecb4, 867d88e; keep both CHANGELOG entries)

RE-GATE PROCEDURE once a rebased head is pushed, #605 first, then #606, in an OPUS session (DEC-182; exit-first respawn or a DEC-183 reviewer unit once adopted). No fork code is fetched, checked out, built or run locally.
1. Read the WHOLE new diff over the API (gh pr diff <n> --repo opum-ai/quest-cli) and confirm it touches no .github/, package.json scripts or dependencies, lockfile, build or test-runner config, or install/lifecycle hooks; if it does, stop and route to opum-doc.
2. Confirm the delta is only the commits already reviewed (605: 9684e29; 606: 0d3ecb4 + 867d88e), modulo conflict resolution; any new content is reviewed on its merits.
3. Approve any held workflow runs on the new head.
4. Run the required-set predicate on the new head: required contexts read from rules/branches/dev, newest row per context all success, AND no row of a required context still pending; read it twice.
5. Report the verdict, head SHA, CI and model id to team-lead BEFORE merging.
6. gh pr merge <n> --squash --match-head-commit <head>, keeping the contributor's authorship; post the outcome comment (technical only, ending with the disclosure line).
7. Repeat for #606, then complete QCLI-497 in a tracker-only PR.

NON-BLOCKING NOTES (posted on the PRs, not asked of the contributor):

- #606 has no test for the Backlog.md import's milestone rebuild order (backlog-public.ts).
- Follow-up idea, not filed: byIdentifier in src/application/planning/planning.ts predates #604 and is a second numeric comparator for milestone and decision lists; folding it into compareTaskIds would leave one comparator.

Result trees verified: 605 tree vs dev differs by exactly 605 own delta (eb929840..9684e294) with CHANGELOG +9 (7 plus a Fixed heading); 606 tree vs resolved 605 differs by exactly 606 own delta (eb929840..867d88e1). CHANGELOG placement: both entries go under Unreleased in a new Fixed heading, NOT in the 0.14.0 section where a literal conflict resolution would land them (0.14.0 is tagged). DEC-181 (2) whole-diff gate on the new heads by gh pr diff --name-only: PASS. 605 touches CHANGELOG.md, src/application/planning/planning.ts, src/application/tasks/tasks.ts, src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts, test/draft-and-milestone-id-order.test.ts. 606 touches those plus src/application/migration/backlog-public.ts and test/milestone-stored-task-order.test.ts. Reviewed #605 dff8b1c490f5d02c403331fe6b259179f5f4132b and #606 e4d4f5b72cea7f9725bcbcafa547f94e23e14993. Verdict file sha256 b49924663745109da27e6db6c0f56ecb14b5680030c58f14a64bbae2feb48fef (verified here). Verbatim:

VERDICT: APPROVE opum-ai/quest-cli#605 at dff8b1c490f5d02c403331fe6b259179f5f4132b. VERDICT: APPROVE opum-ai/quest-cli#606 at e4d4f5b72cea7f9725bcbcafa547f94e23e14993. Both approvals carry the two conditions below, which block MERGE, not approval.

MERGE CONDITIONS
(a) Merge #605 before #606. Otherwise #606 lands #605's code with it (finding M1).
(b) Do not merge either PR into dev until v0.14.1 is tagged from a SHA that excludes them (finding M2).

Reviewer unit, read-only. I read the six scratchpad diffs and the dev tree at 22bc3f08 with Read/Grep only, with no shell and no API.

CHECKS

1. #605 fidelity: CONFIRMED. Outside CHANGELOG.md, q605-approved.diff and q605-new-vs-dev.diff match hunk for hunk, and the blob index lines on both sides are identical:
- planning.ts e588cb89..d7877b7a (@@ -639 and @@ -714)
- application/tasks/tasks.ts 7010dd27..effc7267 (@@ -1043)
- domain/tasks/tasks.ts bbb0e5de..aae18ebc (@@ -1268, docblock)
- test/draft-and-milestone-id-order.test.ts new file 962d6a61
Equal pre-image blobs also show that dev's copies of these files are byte-identical to the approval base eb929840. So each post-image file is exactly what was approved.
CHANGELOG: the bullet text is identical, 7 lines. The approved version was +7 inside an existing ### Fixed at old line 50. The new version is +9 (### Fixed, a blank line, then the bullet) under ## Unreleased. That matches quest-cli's +9 vs +7. Nothing else differs.

2. #606 fidelity: CONFIRMED for #606's own delta. The brief's premise is REFUTED.
- The premise: q606-approved.diff contains NONE of #605's content. It has no planning.ts, no application/tasks.ts and no draft test. Its domain/tasks.ts hunk is only closeMilestoneReference, from base bbb0e5de, not #605's aae18ebc. Its CHANGELOG adds only #606's entry. So at approval, 867d88e1 was a sibling of #605 off eb929840, not stacked on it.
- q606-resolution.diff shows the merge bringing in #605's files: planning.ts e588cb89..d7877b7a, application/tasks.ts 7010dd27..effc7267, and the draft test 962d6a61. The maintainer merge, using dff8b1c4 as second parent, is what stacked #606 on #605.
- So the "approved minus #605" subtraction does not apply. #606's own change is q606-approved.diff as a whole.
- Compared against q606-new-vs-605.diff, it is identical across all 4 files, +67/-2. The brief named 2 of them; all 4 are:
  - CHANGELOG +11: same text, now after #605's bullet under Unreleased / Fixed.
  - src/application/migration/backlog-public.ts +2/-1: 6fb4d99b..59221c97 on both sides, with the import and the sort(compareTaskIds) at @@ -689.
  - src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts +1/-1: identical @@ -1221 hunk (nextTaskIds.sort(compareTaskIds)). The blob is bbb0e5de..05ac10b6 approved vs aae18ebc..c85318cc now. The only difference is #605's docblock already being in the base.
  - test/milestone-stored-task-order.test.ts: new file 6932bb4d on both sides.

3. CHANGELOG: CONFIRMED.
- Both bullets are verbatim.
- #605's diff adds the ### Fixed heading under ## Unreleased, after ### Changed (dev CHANGELOG.md:11-19). #606 appends below it.
- Both hunks end with "## 0.14.0" as unchanged trailing context, so the tagged 0.14.0 section is not touched.
- See M2 for a placement problem the leader's confirmation did not cover.

4. DEC-181 (2): CONFIRMED on both new deltas.
- q605-new-vs-dev.diff has exactly 5 files: CHANGELOG.md, planning.ts, application/tasks/tasks.ts, domain/tasks/tasks.ts and test/draft-and-milestone-id-order.test.ts.
- q606-new-vs-605.diff has exactly 4: CHANGELOG.md, backlog-public.ts, domain/tasks/tasks.ts and test/milestone-stored-task-order.test.ts.
- None touches .github/, package.json, the lockfile, build or test-runner configuration, or install hooks.
- .github/workflows/lore-check.yml, package.json, bun.lock, scripts/* and the npm/* binaries do appear, but only in the two resolution diffs, as dev content. Their index pairs are identical between q605-resolution and q606-resolution (115 vs 119 files; the extra 4 are exactly #605's files).
- Why this is sufficient: dev is a parent of dff8b1c4, so the 5-file new-vs-dev diff proves dff8b1c4 equals dev on every other path. #606 follows by transitivity through its 4-file delta. That rests on the three-dot bases being ancestors, the same caveat as check 5.

5. Authorship and commits: CONSISTENT, but parentage and authorship are UNVERIFIED.
- Diffs carry no parents or authors, so this is inference, not proof.
- q605-resolution (9684e294...dff8b1c4) omits all four #605 code and test files. Its CHANGELOG starts at #605's own blob 80732ede. So the merge-base already contains #605's commit, which implies 9684e294 is an ancestor of dff8b1c4.
- Likewise, q606-resolution omits backlog-public.ts and the milestone test, and its domain/tasks.ts starts at #606's blob 05ac10b6 and its CHANGELOG at f76d2e03. That implies 867d88e1 is an ancestor of e4d4f5b7.
- That is consistent with "merge on top, not rewritten". Confirming the merge commits' two parents and his authorship needs gh api repos/opum-ai/quest-cli/commits/<sha>.

6. Compiles against dev: CONFIRMED by reading.
- compareTaskIds is exported at src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts:1279.
- It is already imported in planning.ts:14 and application/tasks/tasks.ts:6.
- #606 adds it to backlog-public.ts's existing import block from ../../domain/tasks/tasks.ts. Dev's block at lines 16-20 matches the hunk context exactly.
- closeMilestoneReference (:1224) calls a function declaration in the same module, so hoisting is fine.
- The hunk contexts match dev's lines: domain :1220-1224 and :1268-1276.
- The two new test paths do not exist on dev.
- The tests' subcommands exist in the command contract: "draft list" :651, "milestone edit" :699, "cleanup" :849.
- CI source-gates runs 39375815470 and 39375885536 are relayed evidence that I could not read.

FINDINGS
Blocker: none.

Major:
- M1. #606 now carries #605's lines, and they are not conflict lines. They are separately approved and byte-identical, so no unapproved byte entered. But #606 vs dev is now 9 files, not 4, and merging #606 first would land #605's code under #606's squash commit. Remedy: merge-order condition (a), no code change. After #605 lands, confirm #606's diff vs dev shrinks back to the 4 files above. Separately, #606's approval was given on a tree without #605. The combined tree was never reviewed as a unit, though the two changes touch disjoint hunks and the merge was clean.
- M2. The CHANGELOG placement collides with 0.14.1. dev's ## Unreleased currently holds only the 0.14.1 republish note (CHANGELOG.md:15-19): "Only the version strings move here; the code is 0.14.0's." dev's tip 22bc3f08 is the 0.14.1 tag/staging handoff. If either PR lands before v0.14.1 is cut and the tag is taken from a later dev SHA, that bullet and its DEC-204 (2) framing become false, and 0.14.1 would ship code that is not 0.14.0's. This is not a fidelity defect; check 3 holds. It is a sequencing condition, (b): hold the merge until v0.14.1 is tagged from a SHA that excludes these PRs, then expect Unreleased to split into a 0.14.1 section and a fresh Unreleased. I could not check tag state (UNVERIFIED).

Minor:
- m1. Both new tests define a local quest() helper using child.exitCode ?? 0. That is the fold QCLI-502 removed from the whole test tree after his approval base: test/helpers/spawn.ts runCommand, and a grep of dev finds no other instance outside the QCLI-502 prose. Practical risk is low. Neither test reads the returned exitCode, and a killed child gives empty stdout, so JSON.parse throws loudly. This is drift since approval, not a missed review. It is NOT a conflict line, so fixing it inside this resolution would itself break the only-conflict-lines rule. File it as a follow-up.

Nit:
- n1. Both bullets say "builds on the task-id change below". That entry now sits in ## 0.14.0 (CHANGELOG.md:94), not in the same block. It is still literally below. No action.

COULD NOT CHECK WITHOUT A SHELL
- Merge-commit parents and author identity for dff8b1c4 and e4d4f5b7.
- Whether #606's GitHub base branch is dev or #605's branch. This decides what the PR UI shows and how M1 plays out.
- v0.14.1 tag state, and whether its SHA predates these merges.
- Running the tests or typecheck. CI is relayed evidence only.
- That the scratchpad diffs are faithful to the compare API. I trusted the leader's fetch.
